text:
sam: Heads-up — canary on L4 yesterday showed a surprising tail latency regression for short prompts. Kernel selector picked a fallback matmul kernel at seqlen=128 under small-batch conditions.

rachel: ugh. how big was the impact?

sam: ~2.3x P95 for batch=1, seqlen=128 compared to the expected fused kernel. We only see it on L4/T4/A10 variants; A100/H100 keep the fused path. Profiling snippet: 

```
# perf trace (trimmed)
kernel_choice: matmul_fused_v2  -> chosen on h100
kernel_choice: matmul_generic  -> chosen on l4
time_per_token: h100 1.4ms, l4 3.2ms (batch=1, seqlen=128)
KV-cache hit ratio: 0.92
continuous_batching: disabled (policy=min-latency)
```

alex: do we know why selector prefers generic on l4?

sam: autotune scores showed slightly lower memory pressure with generic on a few microbenchmarks (seq=64/256 combos). But those tests had different workspace fragmentation. Seems the selector's cost model underweights kernel startup overhead on small batches for L4.

priya: can we quickly patch selector heuristics to prefer fused for seqlen in [64,192] on ampere-4-like cards? That range seems to regresses.

ben: proposal: add device-class override + a seqlen band to presets. Something like:

```
# runtime presets snippet
device_class: l4_family
kernel_preset_overrides:
  - seqlen_range: [32,192]
    prefer: matmul_fused_v2
```

sam: +1. Also set a short-lived autotune lockdown so we don't retrain weights until we verify perf across workloads.

rachel: need a quick canary. Steps: 1) push preset to canary pool for l4/t4/a10, 2) run bench script `./tools/bench --device l4 --batches 1,4 --seqlen 32,128,512`, 3) collect perf-bot report.

perf-bot: Started benchmark run on pool canary-l4 at 2050031500. Will post summary when done. :gear: 

sam: Timelines — I can author the preset PR today and request reviews. Aim to roll to canary by EOD. If we see no regressions on A100/H100, we can promote to stable next week.

priya: note — also add a regression test in our perf harness that asserts no >1.5x P95 uplift for batch=1 across seqlen grid.

ben: logging note: capture kernel_choice reasons in trace so we can audit future autoselect decisions. e.g., `reason=memory_estimate` vs `reason=startup_cost`.

sam: good call. I'll add the trace fields.

perf-bot: Canary results posted at 2050031705:

```
summary:
  device: l4
  config: preset-l4-fused-seqlen-32-192
  batch=1,seqlen=128: p95 before=3.2ms after=1.45ms (improvement 2.2x)
  batch=4,seqlen=128: p95 before=1.1ms after=1.05ms (no reg on medium batches)
  regressions: none detected on seqlen grid for l4 family
```

rachel: amazing. proceed with rollout to dedicated canaries for client-facing clusters?

sam: yes, will open rollout PR with canary config and changelog. Assigning to @alex for review.

alex: on it. will double-check autotune snapshots to ensure we don't permanently bias away from generic kernels on high-throughput workloads.

priya: I'll add the perf harness assertion and a small test that simulates fragmented workspace to keep autotuner honest.

ben: after rollout, we should run a cross-device sweep (l4,t4,a10,a100,h100) to validate there are no adverse interactions with KV-cache batching heuristics.

sam: agreed. Thanks everyone.

perf-bot: Logged action items: PR # (pending), canary run results attached, follow-up sweep scheduled.
